items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: It was a jazz club run by an American named Dick Edward.

ctx.x: Photos could not be made during the ceremony and it was a good thing, because it was possible for Ollie to begin shooting, he had a camera with flashes that every time he took a photo, the flash made a sound like a bunch of small fire crackers up every time he took a photo. But they came out wonderful.

After,we went to have dinner at Leroy Haynes' place, rue Manuel. Haynes made wonderful "soul food" and we had a ball. We decided afterwards to finish that happy day at the Rind Side, rue Dartois. It was a jazz club run by an American named Dick Edward. Lionel Hampton came, kissed the bride and jammed for hours! That was the end of an hectic but wonderful day for Lily and I.

The tour started the 12th of October, with the first concert taking place in Rouen. We did eleven concerts before playing in Paris at the cinema Clunny the 23rd of October. We did an afternoon concert which was recorded by Pathe-Marconi. A funny thing happened on one number which was not aware of, until I heard the record later. Wallace Bishop had a drum solo on "Lover" which we played two choruses and then left him alone on stage. After about five minutes, we would come back and finish the number with him. This…
